Wide awake at 3:30 am with our nine-year-old daughter on our lodge balcony, I stared for hours at the most incredible night sky I've ever seen before the dawn slowly started to rub out the stars on the horizon and the multiple shooting stars faded away.

sentences.text: Wide awake at 3:30 am with our nine-year-old daughter on our lodge balcony, I stared for hours at the most incredible night sky I've ever seen before the dawn slowly started to rub out the stars on the horizon and the multiple shooting stars faded away.

analysis.translationLiteral: 凌晨三点半，我和九岁的女儿在小屋阳台上毫无睡意，我久久凝视着平生见过的最不可思议的夜空，直到黎明慢慢开始抹去地平线上的星星、众多流星也渐渐消失。
analysis.translationNatural: 凌晨三点半，我和九岁女儿在旅馆阳台上清醒得很；我盯着此生见过最壮丽的星空看了好几个小时，直到天光一点点擦掉地平线上的星子，成群的流星也隐没不见。

paragraphs.text: We were going to my wife's big family reunion in Auckland, New Zealand, but when we found out that Great Barrier Island, just off the coast, had been recently awarded Dark Sky Sanctuary status—a typically remote area that has an "exceptional or distinguished quality of starry nights"—we thought it would be the perfect place to relax before our busy schedule. It's the first island and only the fourth location in the world to achieve this status.

paragraphs.text: After a 28-hour flight with two travel-sick children, our hearts sank when we saw the tiny twin engine 10-seater that was to take us the 90km across the Hauraki Gulf to Great Barrier Island. But we needn't have worried. Whether it was the gravity force of the plane climbing or the noise of the engine, it put our three-year-old daughter instantly to sleep until we bumped down on the grass at Claris Airport. Our first empty sick bag against all the odds…Things were looking up.

sentences.text: But we needn't have worried.

paragraphs.text: Great Barrier Island has no public facilities and the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently) rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking. There are no streetlights. There are no cash machines or banks. The police force comprises a husband and wife, and there's one postman. It's not just the lack of light but the lack of noise that's so delightful on this unique and gorgeous scene. It was first discovered by East Polynesians about 700 years ago and the Maori name for the island is Aotea. Captain Cook gave the island its European name, because it acts as a barrier between the Pacific and the Hauraki Gulf.

sentences.text: Great Barrier Island has no public facilities and the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently) rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking.

analysis.translationLiteral: 大屏障岛没有公共设施，住在那里的 950 人（尽管只有约一半是常住）依靠太阳能和风能，以及做饭用的瓶装燃气。
analysis.translationNatural: 岛上没有公共设施，950 位居民（其中约一半才长期定居）靠太阳能、风能和罐装煤气做饭过日子。
analysis.structMarkup: 【Great Barrier Island】 _has no public facilities_ and 【the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently)】 _rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking_.
analysis.structureSummary: and 连接两个并列分句；前一分句主谓宾，后一分句含现在分词后置定语与括号插入语，rely on 后接并列宾语。

components.note: 本文主角作前一分句主语，谓语用单数 has。
has + 否定宾语，说明岛上缺乏公共设施。

components.part: the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently)
components.note: 后一分句主语；living there 现在分词作后置定语，括号内为省略式插入语补充常住人口。

components.part: rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking
components.note: rely on 后接并列宾语；for cooking 作后置定语修饰 bottled gas。

clauses: 句中含让步/对比连词，引导状语从句；主句不再用 but 呼应。
本句主干为「and 连接两个并列分句；前一分句主谓宾，后一分句含现在分词后置定语与括号插入语，rely on 后接并列宾语。」，先找限定动词再切分修饰成分。

phrases.meaning: 巨大的；很棒的；重要的
phrases.usage: 注意区分：great（巨大/很棒）/ big（大，物理）/ large（大，数量）。常见搭配：a great deal / great importance。
phrases.example: They do not reflect the great mass of behaviour. 它们没有反映行为的主体。

phrases.meaning: 公共的、公众的 / 公众（the public）
phrases.usage: 注意区分：public（公共的）/ pubic（阴部的，拼写易错）。常见搭配：public health / the British public。
phrases.example: Loneliness is a public health problem. 孤独是公共卫生问题。

although/though 引导让步从句时，主句不能再用 but（汉语习惯会说「虽然……但是」）。
analysis.paragraphRole: 以「无公共设施、靠自给能源」勾勒岛屿与世隔绝的底色，为「无光害」作铺垫。

paragraphs.text: The climate here is subtropical(亚热带的) like Auckland's. The island boasts a beautiful wilderness with dense forests, glorious, unspoilt sandy beaches and plenty of bays and a few mountainous areas where there are good walking tracks among the wetlands and valleys. The sheltered western side is where you'll find the best diving and boating. Lots of people come here for the fantastic fishing spots around the island. paragraphs.text: It's rare to find an island that really does feel undiscovered—but this is it. When one of my wife's relations, who comes here regularly, found out that we'd been there, he whispered to us, only half-joking: "Shh—don't tell anyone!" The locals are a relaxed and friendly bunch—a lot of them told us that it's like what Waiheke Island (now in effect a suburb of Auckland) was in the 1970s when it was a commune of artists and people wanting to escape the city.

paragraphs.text: Beginning their astronomical PowerPoint demonstration using a green laser pointer, Hilde and Orla showed us the Messier 4 spherical cluster(星团) with white dwarf stars(白矮星), Saturn and its rings, the Southern Cross and the Milky Way, which stretched across the sky.
